q1.q: Is it a web app, or is there a desktop app?
q1.a: <m>Both.</m> You can use HeyMoa right in your browser, and there's also a desktop app for Mac and Windows. The desktop app records your microphone together with the sound coming from your computer, and shows the Timeline in the menu bar. Either way, you sign in with the same Google account and see the same meeting notes. The Windows version is in beta.

q2.q: Are decisions and tasks final as soon as the meeting ends?
q2.a: No. When you end the meeting, HeyMoa analyzes it and lays everything out in the Summary tab. <m>Decisions and tasks reach the project only after you switch on the ones you want and click Finish review.</m> Anything you leave off stays in the meeting notes. If the meeting is still recording, click Pause first and then end it.

q3.q: What if someone changes their mind mid-meeting?
q3.a: The Timeline doesn't delete the reversed item. It strikes it through and marks it Retracted.

q4.q: What if a line comes out wrong?
q4.a: You can edit or exclude any line, and change a task's assignee and due date. Excluded lines aren't deleted. They stay struck through, and Undo exclude brings them back.

q5.q: What if a new decision overrides an earlier one?
q5.a: The Summary tab attaches a "Replaces an earlier decision" suggestion. To add the new decision to the project, switch it on and choose whether to replace the earlier decision or keep it.
q5.more: See it on the weekly meeting card

q6.q: So what does the note-taker do now?
q6.a: In the Summary tab, fill in any missing assignees and due dates, fix the lines that came out wrong, and <m>click Finish review.</m> Speakers aren't separated during the meeting, so you put names to them in the Transcript tab after it ends.

safety.title: Your meetings reach <m>the tools you use</m>
safety.lead: HeyMoa's built-in agent and the Claude Code or Codex you connect both work from what was said in your meetings.

agent.label: My agent
agent.title: Nothing goes out until you approve it
agent.body: In the same chat where you ask about a meeting, you can ask for a Linear or GitHub issue. Even if the workspace is already connected, it checks with you before creating each one, and tasks from the meeting never move over on their own.

step1.title: An approval card comes first
step1.body: It shows where the issue will go, with its title and description, and waits until you approve or decline.

step2.title: The issue stays in the chat
step2.body: Expand Thinking to find the issue link and the “Approved” record.

agent.figure1: Figure 1 (sample): a My agent chat next to the “Sprint 3 kickoff” meeting notes. Asked to turn the onboarding drop-off logging into a Linear issue, the agent checks first and shows an approval card for creating it. Nothing is sent before you press Approve, and the input box stays locked until then. If you decline, the chat records it as “Declined.”
agent.figure2: Figure 2: the Thinking section of the same chat after approval, with a link to the new issue ONB-12, an Open link, and an “Approved” line.
agent.ask: Make the onboarding drop-off logging a Linear issue
agent.answer: Should I create a Linear issue for this task? Check the details below and approve.

external.label: External agents
external.title: Connect your AI tools and they can look up past meetings
external.body: Connect HeyMoa to an AI tool like Claude Code or Codex, and right where you work it can look up decisions, tasks, and meeting notes, then link you to the HeyMoa screen you need. You create each connection yourself and can disconnect it at any time.
external.figure: Figure: one connection on the My MCP connections screen in settings (sample). Laptop Claude Code is connected, and the expanded usage list shows when it fetched what and how many items. Revoking blocks it from the next request and can't be undone.
external.screenBody: Let AI apps like Claude or ChatGPT read the meetings and projects in a workspace you choose.
external.name: Laptop Claude Code
external.revokeNote: Revoking blocks the very next request, and it can't be undone.
external.logNote: Logs when, what, and how many

worksWith.title: Wherever you meet, just <m>keep HeyMoa on</m>
worksWith.body: Keep the meeting app you already use. HeyMoa doesn't join the call. It listens through your laptop mic from the next tab, so there's no bot to invite and no integration to set up. To record your computer's audio as well, get the <link>desktop app</link>.

zoom.name: Zoom
zoom.line: Open your Zoom call and start a meeting in HeyMoa. The two apps never need to be connected.

meet.name: Google Meet
meet.line: Open one more tab next to Meet. When the meeting ends, decisions and tasks are gathered in the Summary tab.

teams.name: Microsoft Teams
teams.line: HeyMoa never joins the meeting, so no unfamiliar bot shows up in the participant list.

webex.name: Webex
webex.line: It works even if your company chose the meeting app. There's no integration to ask your admin for.

slack.name: Slack huddles
slack.line: Decisions from a quick huddle don't slip away.

discord.name: Discord
discord.line: What you settle in a side-project voice channel gets written down too.

room.name: Meeting room
room.line: Put a laptop in the middle of the table and it captures an in-person meeting with no screen at all.

other.name: Any other app
other.line: Listed here or not, if your laptop can hear it, HeyMoa can write it down.

Then I'll take the onboarding drop-off logging. I'll have a draft up by Thursday.
Great. Let's send that straight to Linear as an issue.
Can we attach today's decision to that issue? So whoever joins next can see it.
Let's look at that when we export it. That's it for today.

meta.title: HeyMoa | Real-time AI meeting notes
meta.description: HeyMoa is an AI agent that carries context from one meeting to the next so your team can decide faster. It takes real-time AI meeting notes, tells speakers apart, and organizes decisions and tasks.
meta.ogImageAlt: HeyMoa — Focus on the meeting and let Moa take the notes. From the live transcript to decisions and tasks, HeyMoa keeps track of how the meeting went.
features: Meeting transcripts with decisions and tasks
The exact quotes behind each decision and task
Team meeting records organized by project
A personal agent that answers from past meetings
Export only what you approve to Linear or GitHub
Connect external agents like Claude Code and Codex
